sections.html: Beloit is a Rock County city on the Rock River, right at the Illinois line, covering 17.3 square miles with 36,649 residents by the July 2025 estimate. Older homes are common. A buyer looking at one will want to hear about the roof, wiring and plumbing, so keep repair records within reach. Investor-owned rentals make up much of the market, and that shapes inspections and timing.

A typical owner-occupied Beloit home is valued at $156,500, and owners live in 59.4% of homes. Median gross rent of $1,066 is high next to those values, which is why investors pay attention to the city.

A building permit is required for new structures, additions, renovations, structural repair and swapping out mechanical systems, and a Certificate of Occupancy follows inspection. New structures, additions and bigger parking lots also face site plan review, and most buildings except one- and two-unit homes go through architectural review. Wrap up permitted repairs before listing so inspections are already signed off.

Landlords get closer attention. The Community and Housing Services Division applies the Housing Property Maintenance Code, inspects rental interiors and does multi-family fire inspections. Selling a rental, with tenants or without, starts with a call to that division about the unit's inspection status. It also operates housing rehabilitation loans that might cover repairs you cannot afford up front.

Stage the paperwork early and closing day gets easier. After you accept an offer, put the lender payoff, the treasurer's balance, any permit sign-offs and the condition report into a single folder for the title company. An open permit found by the buyer's inspector can usually be settled by finishing the inspection.

School boundaries do not always match the city map. Most addresses are in the School District of Beloit, while some parts of the area belong to the Beloit Turner School District. Check a parcel's district before advertising it.

sections.h2: How Beloit assesses a house, and when you can object
sections.html:
Since 2014 the city's assessor has been Tyler Technologies, under contract. Each spring the roll is posted, open book follows, and the Board of Review then meets in the Forum of City Hall. Phone the assessor at 608-364-6670 to get that year's dates.

  • Notice of intent: the City Clerk-Treasurer, at 608-364-6682, needs your name, address, parcel number and a phone number.
  • Do this no later than 48 hours before the board's first meeting.
  • Within the meeting's first two hours, hand in a written objection stating your estimate of land and improvement values.
  • The objection must cover the combined land and improvement value.

The city lays out three steps: speak with the assessor, attend open book, request a Board of Review hearing. Bring your own estimate and any evidence of value to the hearing, and write down what the assessor tells you at open book so you can refer to it later. Beyond the board, the appeal routes in the Department of Revenue's Guide for Property Owners apply.

sections.h2: Paying Beloit property taxes before a sale
sections.html:
Four payments are available to Beloit owners, each one sent to the Rock County Treasurer, on January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31. What goes unpaid is delinquent and gains 1.5% a month from February 1, and a partial month is charged in full. Miss one installment and the entire remainder is delinquent.

The Treasurer's office, 51 South Main Street, Janesville, WI 53545, is open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Call 608-757-5670. GovTech Services handles card payments, charging 2.29% on credit, $3.95 on debit and $1.00 on an e-check. In Beloit, address changes are handled by the Treasurer's Office rather than Real Property.

Ask in writing for your parcel's paid-to-date and balance figures and give them to the title company before closing. When a lender escrows your taxes, check what it has actually paid. A county overpayment returns to the escrow company if the company made the payment, and to you if you paid in person.

The Rock County Register of Deeds records Beloit deeds, takes walk-ins and has a drop box in the Courthouse lobby. A Real Estate Transfer Return must be completed on the Department of Revenue website first, and s. 77.22(1) puts the return and fee ahead of recording.

The county goes by the latest recorded document, so later tax bills carry the buyer's name only once the deed is recorded.

A seller's real estate condition report reaches the buyer within 10 days of contract acceptance (s. 709.02). Anything you learn before acceptance that changes an answer calls for an amended report within 10 days of acceptance (s. 709.035). The form covers structural and mechanical items, as well as taxes, special assessments and permits.

Many Beloit sellers own a rental rather than a home they live in. First decide if the buyer gets the house occupied or vacant, and write that into the contract. Then ask the Community and Housing Services Division about the interior inspection, including any open code items. Fix cheap items before the buyer's inspector sees them, because small findings turn into price cuts.

Hand the buyer the lease, the rent roll and the tenant's contact information, and warn the tenant before each showing. Keep tax bills handy as well. Since every Beloit installment goes to the county, one call to the Treasurer shows what is paid and what remains, which is the number the title company prorates.

The open market, a sale by owner and a cash offer are all open to you. Listing exposes the house to the most buyers and suits one in good condition. A cash buyer takes it as is, useful for inherited property, a tenant in place or repairs costing more than you want to spend.

The tax balance and the condition report must be dealt with on any route. Get a written estimate of your net from the closing agent before accepting an offer, and keep this checklist:

  1. Written paid-to-date tax figure from the Rock County Treasurer.
  2. Permit and inspection status, including any rental inspection.
  3. Completed condition report, delivered on time.
  4. Transfer return filed, with the deed ready to record.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax on a Beloit house?
faqs.a: To the Rock County Treasurer, 51 South Main Street, Janesville. All four City of Beloit installments go to the county: January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31. Questions: 608-757-5670.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Beloit?
faqs.a: About $156,500 for owner-occupied homes (2020 to 2024 estimates), with 59.4% of Beloit homes owner-occupied.

faqs.q: Does Beloit inspect rental houses before a sale?
faqs.a: Yes, the Community and Housing Services Division inspects rental interiors and enforces the Housing Property Maintenance Code. Ask about the unit's status before you list.

faqs.q: When can I protest my Beloit assessment?
faqs.a: Each spring, after the roll is posted for open book. The City Clerk-Treasurer, 608-364-6682, handles the notice of intent and knows the current Board of Review date.

faqs.q: What documents does a Beloit seller owe the buyer?
faqs.a: A finished real estate condition report, within 10 days of contract acceptance. A Real Estate Transfer Return also goes to the Department of Revenue, and the deed is recorded by the Rock County Register of Deeds.
